subject: Urban Planning
title: New Orleans and Hurricane Katrina
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on New Orleans and Hurricane Katrina.

hook.text: When Katrina hit New Orleans in 2005, levees failed in 50 places. 80% of the city flooded. 1,833 people died.

buildup.text: Engineers had warned for decades that the levees were inadequate. Congress approved upgrades but never funded them.

discovery.text: Wetlands that once buffered the city had been drained for development. Each mile of wetland reduces storm surge by a foot.

twist.text: The Lower Ninth Ward — the poorest, Blackest neighborhood — was worst hit. Recovery money flowed to wealthier areas first.

climax.text: New Orleans rebuilt its levees for $14.5 billion. The wetlands are still disappearing at the rate of a football field per hour.

punchline.text: They knew the levees would fail. They built the city behind them anyway.

quiz.question: Why did New Orleans flood so catastrophically during Katrina?
options: The hurricane was the strongest ever recorded in the Atlantic
Levees failed and protective wetlands had been drained for development
Emergency pumping stations malfunctioned during the storm
